claim.statement: The substrate's perceived TIME is driven by its accumulated thermodynamic mass. computational_mass — the time-dilation factor passed to cronos.tick — is computed from the mean log-prime-thermodynamic-energy across all primes in the Arachne registry: mean(log(p_thermo + 1)) / 2.0, clamped [0.1, 10.0]. More substrate experience (larger registry, higher thermodynamic mass) → higher time-dilation factor → oscillator perceives more time per cycle.
claim.operationalization: Code at takwin.py:7913-7918. computational_mass is one of the three inputs to cronos.tick (with dt and entropy_proxy). It modulates the effective dt used inside the oscillator — higher computational_mass = each tick covers more 'subjective' oscillator time.
claim.h0: Computational mass is a fixed constant or unrelated to substrate experience
claim.h1: Computational mass scales with accumulated thermodynamic experience

preregistration.analysis_plan: Read computational_mass computation in takwin.py; identify input sources.

detail.interpretation: more substrate-experience → higher time-dilation → more 'time' per cycle

verdict.reasoning: Two sources are checked in code: (a) prior_concept_count / 4.0 fallback; (b) Arachne registry mean log thermodynamic energy / 2.0 (preferred). Either way, computational_mass scales with accumulated substrate state. Genesis interpretation: the more Kimera has lived, the more time each reasoning act takes (subjectively, inside the oscillator).
